title: Butterfly Kaomoji Ƹ̵̡Ӝ̵̨̄Ʒ: Copy & Paste Butterfly Text Art
meta_description: Copy butterfly kaomoji and text art: the classic Ƹ̵̡Ӝ̵̨̄Ʒ, small ʚїɞ and ʚĭɞ, faces with ʚ ɞ wings like ʚ(˘ᵕ˘)ɞ, and fluttering trails such as *¨*•.¸¸ପଓ.
hero_tagline: Butterflies made from letters, from the ornate Ƹ̵̡Ӝ̵̨̄Ʒ to tiny ʚɞ wings. Tap any butterfly to copy it.
intro: A text butterfly is two mirrored wings with something thin between them. In ʚїɞ the Latin letters ʚ and ɞ are the left and right wings and the Ukrainian letter ї is the body, its two dots standing in for antennae. Ƹ̵̡Ӝ̵̨̄Ʒ is the same plan drawn larger, with Ƹ and Ʒ for the wings and stacked combining strokes giving the body texture. Put a face between the wings and the butterfly becomes a kaomoji, as in ʚ(˘ᵕ˘)ɞ. The trails at the bottom use Oriya and Gujarati letters that look like a pair of wings in flight; phones without those fonts show boxes. The 🦋 emoji is on the animal emoji page.

faq.q: How do you type a butterfly with letters?
faq.a: Use two mirrored letters for wings and one thin character for the body. ʚ and ɞ (U+029A and U+025E) are the usual wings, and ї, ĭ or ϊ goes in the middle, giving ʚїɞ.

It combines Ƹ (U+01B8) and Ʒ (U+01B7) as wings with Ӝ, a Cyrillic letter, as the body. The extra strokes are combining marks layered on each letter, which is why it can look slightly different from one app to the next.

faq.q: Why does ପଓ show as boxes on my phone?
faq.a: ପ and ଓ are Oriya letters, and ઇ is Gujarati. They are used for their wing shapes. A device without fonts for those scripts cannot draw them, so stick to ʚїɞ, which uses Latin and Cyrillic letters.
